title: Self-Supervised Learning from Images with a Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture
layout_note: Three small panels in a row, (a) (b) (c) with bold captions below, each a bottom-to-top diagram on the same grammar: input circles x and y at the bottom, pale encoder/decoder/predictor boxes above them, and an energy box D(.,.) at the top right that the two paths meet in.
grouping: No containers; whitespace and the sub-captions separate the three panels. Each panel keeps the y path on the right and the x path on the left, so equivalent parts line up across panels.
shapes_depth: Flat. Inputs are white circles with a thick dark blue-grey outline and an italic serif letter. Encoders, the decoder and the predictor are borderless rounded rectangles in a very pale blue-grey with grey text. Solid dark arrows go from inputs into encoders; dashed dark arrows carry representations into the energy box. The energy box is the only saturated element: pale pink fill with a thick red outline. In (b) and (c) the latent variable z is a red-outlined circle with a red arrow into the decoder or predictor.
proposed_highlight: Red is spent only on the objective (the D box) and on the latent z, so the eye goes to where the three architectures differ: what is compared (embeddings vs pixels) and whether a conditioned predictor sits between the paths. The paper's own family is the last panel and gets the most specific bold caption.
lesson: Compare architecture families with a shared tiny grammar (input circles at the bottom, pale encoder boxes, one red-outlined objective box at the top), and spend the only accent colour on the objective and the latent, the parts that differ between panels.
notes: venue and year as recorded by Semantic Scholar. Annotation note (2026-11-15): comparison of abstract architecture families rather than the I-JEPA method pipeline itself

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

insights.structure: Three unframed side-by-side schematics captioned (a) Joint-Embedding, (b) Generative, (c) Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture, each built from the same grey encoder boxes so only the changed part differs.
insights.data: Inputs x, y and the conditioning variable z are drawn as circles at the bottom; embeddings s_x, s_y and predictions are italic math labels on the arrows; no real data is shown.
insights.emphasis: Red is reserved for the energy D(.,.) box (red outline, pink fill) at the top of each panel and the red z circle that marks conditioning, so the eye compares where the loss is computed across the three.
insights.flow: Bottom to top: solid arrows from inputs up through encoders, dashed arrows into the red D box at the top right of each panel.
insights.avoid: Grey low-contrast boxes and very thin dashed arrows make the encoders recede; acceptable for an abstract comparison but too faint for a detailed method figure.

arrangement.units: three unframed columns separated by whitespace, each titled by a bold caption beneath it
arrangement.losses_at: top of each panel as a red D(.,.) box
arrangement.shared: x-encoder and y-encoder boxes repeated identically across panels
